source_title: Green Lantern: Every Lantern Color, Ranked From Weakest to Strongest
source_excerpt:
Green Lantern Hal Jordan arrived in the DC Universe with Showcase #22 in October of 1959, and it changed DC forever. Alan Scott was the original Green Lantern , but Hal took the concept in a more cosmic direction rather than the mystical adventures that were Alan's wheelhouse. Green Lanterns were the only Lantern Corps for quite a while, as Sinestro and Star Sapphire were solo operators without their own Corps at the time.
However, things changed in the 2000s, and the Green Lantern corner of the DC Universe exploded with Lantern colors from every shade of the rainbow and beyond. With some exceptions, each of these colors is tied to an overriding emotion. Many of the Lantern colors share abilities, but most of them have a unique ability that sets them apart from the other shades. Some of them are much more powerful than others, with Green Lanterns not even being the most powerful Lantern color anymore.
13 The Mauve Lantern Exists to be a Gag for Ambush Bug and Lobo
There have been two Mauve Lanterns in DC Comics. One is from Ambush Bug: Year None #2 and had the secret identity of Don Gaye Apparel. He was the herald for an entity called Mr. Nebula, who was some sort of cosmic being overseeing fashion. The more recent Mauve Lantern appeared in Lobo #3 (2026) and went by the name Francis Dalex.
The more recent Mauve Lantern flunked out of being a Green Lantern, but his overwhelming happiness transformed his Green Lantern ring into the Mauve Lantern ring. He had the misfortune of visiting Czarnia before its demise and meeting a young Lobo. Even back then, Lobo was a hell-raiser, and he used one of his hooked chains to steal the Mauve Lantern ring and the finger to which it was attached. Lobo took the ring on a joyride. The Mauve Lantern ring didn't show much for itself, and the two Mauve Lanterns there have had little impact.
12 The Blue Lanterns Can Only Reach Their True Potential With Green Lanterns
The Blue Lanterns first appeared in Green Lantern #25 in 2008. This Corps stands for the emotion of hope. They were founded by Ganthet, one of the Guardians of the Universe, to be a companion Corps to the Green Lanterns. Consequently, the Blue Lantern ring only reaches its true potential in the presence of a Green Lantern.
The Blue Lantern ring can power up a Green Lantern ring, so a Blue Lantern cannot take full advantage of the ring unless there is a Green Lantern present. Without a Green Lantern present, it has been said that a Blue Lantern is weaker. Beyond that, the Blue Lantern ring can also heal others, including purging them of fear or restoring a Red Lantern to their natural selves. While the Blue Lantern has its perks, the reliance on the Green Lanterns holds them back.
11 The Sorrow Lantern Can Infect Others With Sadness
Nathan Broome, who made his first appearance in Green Lantern #2 (2023), was the fiancé Carol Ferris before Hal Jordan once again came back to her life. This ultimately led Carol to leave Nathan for Hal, and this devastated Nathan. With the emotional spectrum fractured at the time, this outpouring of emotion led to Nathan becoming the Sorrow Lantern.
This ring can do most everything a Green Lantern can do, but it also leaves its user in a perpetual state of sadness. The Sorrow Lantern can also infect others with its sadness, which is debilitating to its victims. He went after the Green Lantern Corps in his grief over losing Carol. Nathan Broome is the only known Sorrow Lantern so far, and he met his demise during the Starbreaker Crisis.
10 Star Sapphires Can Heal and Crystallize With the Power of Love
Star Sapphires, sometimes known as Violet Lanterns, are warriors powered by love. They are primarily represented by Hal Jordan's on-again, off-again love interest, Carol Ferris. Carol Ferris made her first appearance alongside Hal in Showcase #22 in 1959. She would later become Star Sapphire in Green Lantern #16 in 1962.
The Star Sapphires can do most of what the Green Lanterns can do with a few extra perks. The Star Sapphires can heal others and put a target in a crystalline prison. Some can even induce a feeling of love in others, and they can form a tether across vast distances of space to their own lover. Unlike prior entries, the Star Sapphires are real powerhouses on par with the Green Lantern Corps.
9 The Yellow Lantern Ring Harnesses the Power of Fear
The Yellow Lanterns, also known as the Sinestro Corps, made their debut in Green Lantern #10 in 2006. As one can tell from the name, this Corps formed around Thaal Sinestro, arch-enemy of Hal Jordan and the Green Lantern Corps. The Yellow Lantern ring harnesses the power of fear and can make that fear manifest for its enemies.
The Yellow Lantern ring can also create fear in others, which can be debilitating. It also has the surprising ability to empower a Kryptonian if used properly. Beyond that, the Yellow Lantern ring can do just about anything a Green Lantern ring can do. This includes making an energy "twin" and limited time travel. At one point, the color yellow was one of the Green Lanterns' weaknesses, and this gave Sinestro and his followers an edge over the Green Lanterns in battle.
8 The Red Lantern Ring Replaces the Need for a Heart
The Red Lantern Corps made their first appearance in Green Lantern #25 in 2008. Led by Atrocitus, this Corps is driven by an overwhelming rage. The ring replaces their need for a heart, pumping red-hot blood through the user's veins that can be vomited onto others like burning napalm. The ring also heals the Lantern and makes them very hard to kill. It also allows them to make blood portals and gives limited telepathy.
The Red Lanterns would be higher on this list if there were not some drawbacks. Due to replacing the heart, removal of the Red Lantern ring can be fatal to its host. It takes a Blue Lantern to restore a Red Lantern to their old selves. The ring also leaves its host mindless and feral until their mind can be restored. There is also the inconsistency of whether a Red Lantern can make constructs, as this was a primary plot point of the Peter Milligan and Ed Benes' Red Lanterns comic book series. It took a human becoming a Red Lantern before the Corps could make constructs, but there had also been comics before this point that showed Red Lanterns making constructs. The continuity is a little inconsistent here.
7 The Green Lantern Ring is Powered by Sheer Will
The Green Lantern Corps represents the power of will. It was the first emotion to emerge and was the first Lantern Corps. In many ways, it's the "vanilla" Lantern Corps, as the rings of the other Lantern Corps can largely do the same things as the Green Lanterns with some bonuses. However, it can't be denied that the Green Lantern Corps has shown its strength and its ability to keep the other Corps in line many times over the years. In addition, it has allowed Hal to take on powerful enemies such as Hector Hammond , Mongul, and the Shark.
That said, there are a couple of rare powers that the Green Lanterns have shown over the years that are not shared by every other Corps. They can turn invisible, phase through walls, create an energy "twin," provide limited time travel, and the ring has shown the ability to preserve or even restore life in the past. Collecting multiple rings turned Hal Jordan into a godlike figure when he became the villainous Parallax. The Green Lanterns have also been the most resilient Corps, as the other Lantern Corps have been brought to the brink of destruction in recent years while the Green Lanterns are still going strong .
6 The Orange Lantern Ring Provides an Entire Army
The Orange Lantern Corps represents avarice (greed); it is also made up of only one Lantern. The current Orange Lantern is named Larfleeze, and he has been driven to madness by the ring. However, the ring has also made him uniquely powerful. The biggest perk of the Orange Lantern ring is the ability to summon the Orange Lantern's victims as energy constructs to do their bidding.
Having an army at command is a potent ability, and it has given Larfleeze the edge in battle countless times. In addition, the Orange Lantern ring can do just about everything the other lanterns can do, including flight, force fields, energy constructs, and energy blasts. The Orange Lantern Corps also made its first appearance in Green Lantern #25 in 2008.
5 The Indigo Lantern Ring Can Channel the Power of Other Colors
The Indigo Tribe is considered the hidden Corps, as they mostly keep to themselves. Members of the Indigo Tribe are forcibly reformed killers and criminals. The Indigo Lantern ring represents compassion and imbues the feeling in anyone who is chosen by the object. The Indigo ring offers a lot of power, but it must be used as the ring wills it, not the wielder.
What makes the Indigo Tribe more powerful than the other Lantern Corps is the Indigo light's ability to mimic the powers of the other Lantern Corps. This means the Indigo Tribe can do anything the other Lantern Corps can do by taking on their aspects. The Indigo Tribe made its debut in Green Lantern #25 in 2008.
4 The Phantom Lantern Can Swap Colors at Will
The Phantom Lanterns made their debut in Green Lanterns #8 in 2016. The first known Phantom Lantern was Frank Laminski, a man who wanted more than anything in the world to be a Green Lantern, but he was never chosen. However, he was found by the remnants of Volthoom, the First Lantern. Volthoom had access to all colors of the emotional spectrum, and the Phantom Lantern ring gave Frank access to it all.
This means that the Phantom ring can completely change colors in a way that even the Indigo Tribe cannot. The drawback is that the Phantom Lantern ring causes the user to overflow with their chosen emotion, and this can eventually lead them to detonate. After Frank was apprehended, Cyborg Superman briefly had the Phantom Lantern ring, and he used it to terrorize Green Lanterns Simon Baz and Jessica Cruz.
